newsitem.title: GERMANY: How proposed German taxes would look.
newsitem.headline: How proposed German taxes would look.

text.p: Following is itemised list of main changes proposed in tax reform plan approved by German coalition parties on Thursday.
The tax reform would take effect over two years in 1998 and 1999. 1. Overall impact:
Tax cuts due to lower rates: 81.95 billion marks.
Reduction of tax breaks: 38.12 billion.
Net reduction in state revenues: 43.83 billion.
NOTE - Net tax reduction planned at around 30 billion marks, with remainder to be financed by an as-yet undecided increase in Germany's 15 percent rate of value added tax.
In addition, tax revenues will be reduced by 7.5 billion marks resulting from a cut in 1998 in the solidarity surcharge to 5.5 percent from 7.5 percent. 2. Tax rates:
From 1999, the single person's income tax-free up to 13,014 marks/year (26,028 for married couple).
Income up to 18,035 marks (36,071 marks) taxed at 15 percent.
Income up to 90,017 marks (180,035 marks) taxed on sliding scale rising from 22.5 percent to 39 percent.
Top-rate tax on commercial income will fall from 47 percent to 40 percent in 1998, and to 35 percent in 1999.
Corporation tax will also fall to 40 percent and then 35 percent on retained profits, and to 28 percent and 25 percent on profits paid to shareholders.
Capital earnings tax falls to 15 percent in 1999.
Tax on interest discount falls to 25 percent in 1999. 3. Counter-financing:
Increased revenues are based on current tax code and are worth 50.8 billion marks. Under the planned tax system the revenues would be 25 percent lower.
i) Employees:
-- Travel allowance falls to 0.40 marks/km from 0.70 marks/km. Journeys to work of over 15 km deductible. (extra revenues 4.2 billion marks).
-- Reduction in personal expenses allowance to 1,300 marks from 2,000 marks (+3.9 billion).
-- No tax relief on Sunday, holiday and night work (+2.2 billion).
-- Halving in top personal insurance allowance to 3,000 marks (+1.1 billion).
-- No tax allowances on severance pay (+0.9 billion)
-- Abolition of range of employee tax exemptions, including travel costs, payments for birth, marriage or company jubilees etc (+0.75 billion).
-- Taxing half of supplementary benefits like unemployment pay and short-time working pay (+0.3 billion).
ii) Savings and life insurance:

-- Interest on capital life insurance, whose contributions can be set against tax, will be taxed at 10 percent yearly or at maturity. Ruling applies to policies started before January 23, 1997 only from the year 2001. (+3.4 billion).
-- Halving of interest free allowance for savers to 3,000 marks (+2.1 billion).
iii) Pensions:

-- Pensions towards which employers pay half of the contributions tax-free are liable to tax on 50 percent of their volume. Monthly pensions above 2,600 marks (5,200 marks for married couples) will be liable to tax.
-- Other pensions liable to tax on 30 percent of their volumes (together +1.5 billion).
iv) Capital gains tax, rents:
-- Abolition of writeoffs on private buildings (+2.4 billion).
-- Speculation threshold lengthened to 10 from two years (+1.2 billion).
-- Speculation threshold lengthened on share dealings to one year (+30 million).
-- Higher taxes on selling shares in Kapitalgesellschaften, a form of company (+0.5 billion).
v) Abolition of corporate tax breaks:
-- Introduction of tax on rises in carrying value of assets (+5 billion).
-- Abolition of reserves set against threatened losses (+5 billion).
-- Limits on reserves against losses in insurance industry (+1.3 billion).
-- Reduction in writedowns on moveable assets by five percent (+4.3 billion).
-- Reduction on normal writedowns for buildings (+1.8 billion).
-- Reduction on special writedowns for small- and medium-sized companies (+1 billion).
-- Abolition of special exemptions for agriculture and forestry (+0.6 billion).
